Supplementary Information

Figure S1. X-ray diffraction patterns of products obtained by the same solid-state synthesis

conditions with varied contents of CaO and Ca(OH)2 in the precursors. Calculated Bragg reflection

positions of Ca1.5Ba0.5Si5O3N6 are shown by green vertical tick marks. Peaks in the grey band

regions are from impurities and those marked with asterisks are identified as CaSi2O2N2.


<!-- Page 3 -->

Figure S2. X-ray diffraction patterns of solid-state synthesis products when using different ball

mill materials: stainless steel (black), zirconia (red), tungsten carbide (blue). Calculated Bragg

positions of Ca1.5Ba0.5Si5O3N6 are shown by green vertical tick marks. Peak in the grey band

regions is from the impurity Fe (BCC polymorph) and those in pink regions are from ZrN.

Figure S3. Rietveld refinement of time-of-flight neutron powder diffraction patterns of (a) Bank

2, (b) Bank 4, (c) Bank 5, (d) Bank 6 at 290 K. Calculated positions of Bragg reflections of CBSON

are shown by green vertical tick marks.


<!-- Page 5 -->


-5-

Figure S4. Rietveld refinement of neutron powder diffraction pattern for CBSON at (a) 475 K,

(b) 3 K. The experimental data are shown as black circles, the red line denotes the calculated

pattern, and the difference profile is shown in blue underneath. Calculated positions of Bragg

reflections are shown by green vertical tick marks. The two peaks marked with asterisk are from

the impurity Fe (BCC polymorph) due to the use of stainless steel as ball mill media in the synthesis

of this batch. The impurity regions are excluded in the refinement.

Figure S5. Nuclear density iso-surface plot from MEM analysis of NPD at 475 K through the

<010> direction at (a) Si-N layer; (b) Ba layer (surface threshold, 0.03 fm/Å3). The Si, N and Ba

atoms are represented by blue, grey and green balls, respectively. It indicates that the nuclear

densities around Ba, Si and N atoms are highly localized.


<!-- Page 6 -->

Figure S6. Full chemical potential triangle for CBSON used to determine the range of chemical

potentials over which to evaluate defect formation (Figure 3b). The green region indicates the

range of chemical potentials where CBSON is thermodynamically stable.

Figure S7. Log-log plots of MSD vs. time. The dotted black line indicates a slope of unity.

Figure S9. Ca-ion probability density of CBSON with one static vacancy from AIMD simulation

at 1500 K down the [010] direction. Isosurface thresholds are: (a) 0.01 eV/ Å3; (b) 0.001 eV/ Å3;

(c) 0.0001 eV/ Å3. (d) Ca-ion probability density of Ca layer without static vacancy (isosurface

threshold is 0.0001 eV/ Å3).
